purge -- Purge records from catalog

USAGE
  purge [catalog=<catalog>]
  purge files [job=<job>] [jobid=<jobid>[,...]] [client=<client>] [volume=<volume>] [yes]
  purge jobs [client=<client>] [volume=<volume>] [pool=<pool>] [jobstatus=<jobstatus>[,...]] [yes]
  purge volume[=<volume>] [all] [pool=<pool> | allpools] [volstatus=<volstatus>[,...]] [volume=<volume> ...] [storage=<storage>] [devicetype=<devicetype>] [drive=<drive>] [action=<truncate|all>] [dryrun | yes]
  purge quota [client=<client>] [yes]

DESCRIPTION
  Deletes catalog records without regard to retention periods. It needs full access to every resource.

  purge volume all (Onesimus extension) purges every volume of one pool (pool=) or of all pools the console may access (allpools) whose status is one of volstatus= (default Full,Used,Error). It is never interactive: dryrun only shows what would be purged, yes purges.

SUBCOMMANDS
  purge files
      File records

      Deletes file records from the catalog regardless of retention periods, for one job (job= or jobid=), a client or a volume; the jobs themselves stay. Like every purge it prints a warning, needs full access to all resources and cannot be undone.

      Onesimus deviation: the file records of the latest Full chain of a client and FileSet are skipped, and each purge runs in one transaction whose errors are reported instead of ignored.
  purge jobs
      Job records

      Deletes whole jobs with all their records regardless of retention periods, for a client, a volume or a pool. jobstatus= limits this to jobs with the given status letters (T, E, f, ...) or names such as error, separated by commas. The Director counts the jobs and asks Purge (yes/no)? unless yes is given. A volume left without jobs becomes Purged.

      Onesimus deviation: jobs of the latest Full chain of a client and FileSet are skipped, and each purge runs in one transaction whose errors are reported.
  purge volume[=<volume>]
      Volume records

      Deletes every job on a volume from the catalog regardless of retention; the volume then becomes Purged and can be reused. Several volume= may be given, and each is confirmed on its own unless yes is given. action=truncate or all runs the ActionOnPurge on Purged volumes through the Storage Daemon, with storage=, pool= or allpools, devicetype= and drive=. A volume holding the latest Full chain of a client is never purged (Onesimus).

      Onesimus extension: purge volume all purges every volume of pool= or of all permitted pools (allpools) whose status is in volstatus=, by default Full, Used and Error. Purged and Recycle volumes are never selected and Cleaning tapes cannot be purged. It never asks: exactly one of dryrun (preview) and yes is required, and refused volumes are skipped with their reason.
  purge quota
      Quota of a client

      Resets the quota counters of a client; without client= the client is chosen from a list. Like every purge it prints a warning and needs full access to all resources.

ARGUMENTS
  purge
    catalog=<catalog>
        Catalog name (name; values from .catalogs)
  purge files
    job=<job>
        Job name (name; values from .jobs)
    jobid=<jobid>[,...]
        Job IDs (text; several values separated by commas)
    client=<client>
        Client name (name; values from .clients)
    volume=<volume>
        Volume name (name; values from .media)
    yes
        Do not ask (keyword)
  purge jobs
    client=<client>
        Client name (name; values from .clients)
    volume=<volume>
        Volume name (name; values from .media)
    pool=<pool>
        Pool name (name; values from .pools)
    jobstatus=<jobstatus>[,...]
        Job status letters (text; several values separated by commas)
    yes
        Do not ask (keyword)
  purge volume[=<volume>]
    volume[=<volume>]
        Volume name (name; values from .media; the value may be left out)
    all
        Every volume of the pool selection (Onesimus) (keyword)
    pool=<pool>
        Pool name (name; values from .pools; excludes the other arguments of group scope)
    allpools
        Every pool (keyword; excludes the other arguments of group scope)
    volstatus=<volstatus>[,...]
        Volume status (Onesimus); Purged and Recycle volumes are never selected, Cleaning tapes cannot be purged (one of a fixed set; values: Full, Used, Error, Append, Archive, Disabled, Read-Only; several values separated by commas)
    volume=<volume> ...
        Volumes for action= (several allowed) (name; values from .media; may be repeated)
    storage=<storage>
        Storage name (name; values from .storages)
    devicetype=<devicetype>
        Device type (text)
    drive=<drive>
        Drive number (number)
    action=<truncate|all>
        Action on purge (one of a fixed set; values: truncate, all)
    dryrun
        Only show what would be purged (Onesimus) (keyword; excludes the other arguments of group mode)
    yes
        Do not ask (keyword; excludes the other arguments of group mode)
  purge quota
    client=<client>
        Client name (name; values from .clients)
    yes
        Do not ask (keyword)

EXAMPLES
  purge volume=Full-0001 yes
      purge one volume
  purge volume all pool=Full volstatus=Full,Used dryrun
      show what would be purged (Onesimus)
  purge volume all allpools yes
      purge every Full, Used or Error volume (Onesimus)
  purge
      choose what to purge from the menu
  purge jobs client=bareos-fd jobstatus=E
      purge the failed jobs of bareos-fd
  purge files jobid=599
      purge the file records of job 599
  purge files client=bareos-fd yes
      purge all file records of bareos-fd
  purge jobs volume=Full-0001 yes
      purge every job on volume Full-0001
  purge jobs pool=Incremental jobstatus=E,f
      purge the failed jobs of pool Incremental
  purge volume action=truncate storage=File pool=Full
      truncate the purged volumes of pool Full
  purge volume all pool=Incremental volstatus=Error dryrun
      preview purging the Error volumes of Incremental (Onesimus)
  purge quota client=bareos-fd
      reset the quota of bareos-fd

ORIGIN
  Bareos console command.

SEE ALSO
  prune, delete, truncate
